catalog.title: Providers
catalog.description: Common natural hazard data sources. Commercial providers connect through an HTTPS endpoint in the app's hazard API format (a contract and, if needed, a translation service at the provider are required). Coverage per vendor information, October 2026.

notes.screening: Weather-based approximation from Open-Meteo climate data plus GDV hail zones. Not a catastrophe model.
notes.zuers: GDV zoning for flood and heavy rain. Detected automatically in the regular location import.
notes.catnet: Multi-peril data from Swiss Re for locations worldwide.
notes.munichre: Scores incl. hail, lightning, river flood, storm surge and earthquake (formerly NATHAN).
notes.moodys: Risk scores and average annual loss (AAL) for more than 100 countries.
notes.verisk: Europe: windstorm and severe thunderstorm/hail (22 countries), inland flood for Central Europe incl. Germany.
notes.jba: Flood specialist; Germany map at 5 m resolution for river and surface water.
notes.fathom: Global flood maps for river, pluvial and coastal flooding.
notes.custom: Any other service that answers in the app's hazard API format – e.g. your own translation service.
notes.jrc: Free EU flood hazard maps (100 m, return periods 10–500 years). Not integrated yet.

connector.contract: The endpoint receives POST {latitude, longitude, perils} with a bearer token and must return {hazards: [{peril, score 0–100, …}]}. Only the location's coordinates are sent.

hailEalDetail.title: Hail EAL

vehicleSource.assetValue: Vehicle count derived from the declared asset value.

zoneSource.postcode: Hail zone from the postcode table.
zoneSource.provider: Hail zone derived from the NatCat provider score.
zoneSource.estimated: Hail zone estimated from weather data (no postcode zone).

hailEalDetail.legacy: Scored with an older model ({{eal}}). Choose “Recalculate” on the dashboard to get the hail EAL.

hailEal.what: Expected hail loss per year (expected annual loss) for the locations shown.
hailEal.how: EAL = N × λ × (p_S·S_S + p_M·S_M + p_L·S_L). N = vehicles parked in the open, λ = hail events per year by hail zone, p = share of small/medium/large events, S = loss per vehicle. Values under “Parameters → Hail EAL”.
hailEal.limits: λ, p, and S are uncalibrated placeholders. A screening estimate, not a tariff, underwriting, or insurance decision.

accumulations.what: Groups of locations that a single hail event could hit together – sorted by exposure.
accumulations.how: Two locations belong together when they are at most {{radius}} km apart; neighbors form chains (single linkage). Loss scenario = accumulation exposure × {{scenario}} damage ratio.
accumulations.limits: The radius is an assumption about the typical size of a hail cell; storm tracks and weather situations are not modeled. The loss scenario is not a PML from a catastrophe model.

zones.what: How locations or exposure spread across hail zones 1 (low) to 6 (very high).
zones.how: Zone from the postcode hail-zone table; without a postcode it is estimated from the weather-based hail score (shown in the tooltip).
zones.limits: Hail zones describe regional hazard, not the condition of the individual site.

topLocations.what: The locations with the highest expected hail loss per year.
topLocations.how: Sorted by hail EAL (€/year). The badge shows the hail zone; “≈” = estimated zone.
topLocations.limits: The EAL depends strongly on the vehicle count – manually reviewed counts improve the ranking.

review.what: Locations an underwriter should look at more closely, with the rule that raised the note.
review.how: Critical: hail zone ≥ {{zone}}; share of the portfolio EAL ≥ {{share}}; accumulation within {{radius}} km with exposure ≥ {{threshold}}. Data quality: utilisation > {{utilisation}}, boundary confidence ≤ {{confidence}}, 0 detected vehicles, estimated hail zone. Thresholds under “Parameters”.
review.limits: Rule-based and unweighted – a note is a request to review, not a decline.
